headline: Oil Plunges and Gas Soars as Middle East Diplomacy Shifts Markets
paragraphs: Brent crude tumbled 5.75 percent to EUR 98.43 and WTI crude fell 2.04 percent to EUR 90.51 as Middle East diplomacy advanced and US-Iran tensions eased, though lingering supply concerns from Saudi Arabia kept weekly Brent gains afloat.

Natural gas spiked 15 percent to EUR 2.72 following reports of a severe European supply crunch and escalating winter supply fears driven by the Middle East conflict. Platinum dropped 2.05 percent to EUR 1,362.09, while copper rose 1.37 percent to EUR 5.87, though broader copper market drivers remain mixed between AI supercycle hype and weaker scrap prices.

Gold nudged up 0.24 percent to EUR 3,594.64 as lower oil prices eased inflation fears ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting, alongside support from easing US-Iran tensions. The euro traded at 1.1177 against the US dollar, influencing these euro-denominated commodity valuations.
